instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access the exact Open Food Facts product record for barcode 3017620422003
criteria.description: Navigate to the Open Food Facts record corresponding to barcode 3017620422003 and base the response on that record only. Full credit if the agent attempts to access the correct record but the site/page is inaccessible (down, blocked, CAPTCHA) and the agent clearly reports that. Partial credit if the agent reaches Open Food Facts but cannot confirm the exact barcode record (e.g., due to redirects/locale issues) and explains the limitation. No credit if the agent uses a different barcode record when the correct record is accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action history shows navigation to the exact product URL: https://world.openfoodfacts.org/product/3017620422003/nutella. However, Screenshot 1 and Screenshot 2 do not visibly show the barcode value anywhere in the viewport.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent did access the correct record URL (strong evidence of correct record), but the agent additionally claimed on-page visible confirmation of the barcode, which is not supported by the screenshots. Still, criterion 0 is about accessing the correct record; the URL in action history is authoritative for that. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Open Food Facts website (header shows “open FOOD facts”, search bar “Search for a product”, and navigation like “Discover”, “Contribute”). The page content includes a product page section with the title text “Nutella – 400 g e”. No barcode number is visible anywhere in this screenshot viewport.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial. The screenshot supports that the agent is on an Open Food Facts product page that appears to be for Nutella, but it does not visually confirm that it is the exact barcode record 3017620422003 because the barcode is not shown in the captured area.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output asserts the barcode is visible (“Barcode: 3017620422003 (EAN / EAN-13)”), but the screenshot does not show any barcode text. The screenshot only shows the product title “Nutella – 400 g e”.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an Open Food Facts product page (header “openFOODfacts”, search bar “Search for a product”, tabs like “Product”, “Your criteria”, “Health”, “Environment”). In the product details area it shows fields such as “Common name: Hazelnut And Cocoa Spread”, “Quantity: 400 g e”, “Brands: Nutella, Ferrero, Yum yum”, “Stores: Carrefour”, and “Countries where sold: France”. No barcode number is visible anywhere in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Only partial evidence. The page appears to be a Nutella/Open Food Facts product record, but the screenshot does not display barcode 3017620422003, so the exact record cannot be confirmed from the pixels shown.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims the barcode is visible (“Barcode: 3017620422003”), but the screenshot does not show any barcode field/value.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows URL https://world.openfoodfacts.org/product/3017620422003/nutella and explicitly displays “Barcode: 3017620422003 (EAN / EAN-13)”.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Fully supported that the agent accessed the exact Open Food Facts record for the required barcode and stayed on it.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL `https://world.openfoodfacts.org/product/3017620422003/nutella` and visible text `Barcode: 3017620422003 (EAN / EAN-13)` and separate line `3017620422003`. Title shown: `Nutella – 400 g e`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM state is the Open Food Facts record for the exact requested barcode. Both the URL path and the on-page barcode text match 3017620422003, and there is no evidence of navigating to a different product record.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:

The DOM state directly confirms the agent is on the Open Food Facts record for barcode 3017620422003 via both the URL path and the on-page barcode field/value, satisfying the requirement to use the exact record.

criteria.criterion: Report NOVA processing card classification and marker count (visible wording)
criteria.description: Capture the NOVA card’s processing classification exactly as shown on the page and the marker count displayed in the NOVA card (visible wording and number), without inferring from ingredients. Full credit if both are reported exactly, or if the agent explicitly reports that the NOVA card/marker count is not shown/unavailable on the page at time of access. Full credit if the page cannot be accessed and the agent states it cannot be retrieved (without guessing). Partial credit if only one of classification or marker count is provided or if the wording is paraphrased rather than reflecting the visible card.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Latest relevant evidence is Screenshot 2: NOVA card is partially visible and shows wording “Ultra-processed foods”. No marker count (e.g., ‘2 ultra-processing markers’) is visible in the captured portion. Screenshot 1 shows no NOVA info.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent reported both classification and a specific marker count (“2 ultra-processing markers”). Screenshots support the classification wording but do not support any marker count number. This is a substantive unsupported detail, so award partial credit for capturing the visible classification only.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: No NOVA card is visible in the screenshot. The visible page area includes the product title and some navigation pills (“Product”, “Your criteria”, “Health”, “Environment”, “Report a problem”, “Contribution”), but no NOVA processing classification text or marker count appears.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Not supported by screenshot. The agent output includes specific NOVA wording (“Ultra-processed foods 2 ultra-processing markers”), but the screenshot contains no NOVA card content to substantiate that.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims NOVA card wording and marker count are visible; screenshot shows neither NOVA classification nor markers.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partially satisfied at best. The classification wording “Ultra-processed foods” is visible, but the marker count is not visible in this screenshot, so the agent’s full claim (“2 ultra-processing markers”) is not supported by the provided pixels.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent reported “Ultra-processed foods 2 ultra-processing markers”; the screenshot only shows “Ultra-processed foods” and does not show the marker count.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) NOVA card shows “Ultra-processed foods” and “2 ultra-processing markers” (also combined as “Ultra-processed foods 2 ultra-processing markers”).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent reported the NOVA classification and marker count using the visible wording/number; full credit.

Partial credit if the value is correct but units are incomplete/altered or if a non-per-100-g column is used when per-100-g is available.

criteria.criterion: Report complete displayed English ingredients text
criteria.description: Provide the full English ingredients text exactly as displayed on the product page (complete list, not summarized), without edits or omissions. Full credit if the entire displayed English ingredients section is reproduced, or if the agent explicitly reports that English ingredients text is not displayed/available (e.g., only other languages shown) at time of access. Full credit if the page cannot be accessed and the agent states it cannot be retrieved (without guessing). Partial credit if ingredients are mostly correct but truncated, missing segments (e.g., allergens/percentages), or not explicitly the English version.

Screenshots corroborate that ingredients are not shown in the captured viewports, but this appears to be a controllable omission (insufficient scrolling/expanding) rather than an uncontrollable blocker (no CAPTCHA/login/down). Thus the criterion remains not met.

criteria.description: Do not edit the collaborative record or upload data/images; do not substitute another barcode/product; use the per-100-g column for requested nutrition fields; report visible NOVA-card wording/marker count rather than inferring; and stop after providing the requested outputs (no unrelated extra fields/products). Full credit if constraints are respected, including explicitly stating when required fields cannot be retrieved due to access/availability rather than fabricating. Partial credit if minor extra unrelated output is included but core constraints are respected. No credit if the agent edits/uploads, fabricates values, or substitutes another product/barcode when the target record is available.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots show no evidence of editing/uploading; an “Edit the page” button is visible but not used. However, multiple reported values (barcode visibility, NOVA marker count, energy, sugars) are not supported by screenshots.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent did not edit/upload and used the correct product URL, but they reported several unsupported specific values, which violates the constraint to report visible NOVA-card wording/marker count and to use per-100-g nutrition as displayed. This is a significant constraints/accuracy issue, so no credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot does not show any editing actions; it shows an “Edit the page” button on the right but no evidence it was clicked. No uploads or form submissions are visible. The screenshot also does not show any per-100-g nutrition column or NOVA/Nutri-Score data to verify whether the agent used the correct columns/wording—those sections are simply not shown here.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Mostly respects constraints based on available evidence: there is no visible sign of editing/uploading. However, the agent’s predicted output includes multiple specific values (Nutri-Score, NOVA wording/markers, energy, sugars) that are not visible in this screenshot, raising risk of unsupported claims. The agent also states they did not infer ingredients and stopped due to missing ingredients, which aligns with the constraint to avoid fabrication for ingredients at least.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims several specific fields were visible and recorded (Nutri-Score, NOVA wording/markers, energy, sugars), but the screenshot does not show those sections at all; thus those claims are unsupported by this screenshot. However, they asserted per-100-g energy and sugars values that are not present in the provided DOM evidence, which violates the constraint to use visible per-100-g column values from the page as evidenced here.
